blocks.heading: The longer story
blocks.body: Who I am, how I got here, how I work and what I am building — the parts a resume leaves out.

blocks.heading: My story
blocks.body:
I studied **Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning** at J.B. Institute of Technology (Uttarakhand Technical University), and joined **VA2PT** as a DevOps trainee in July 2025, a month before graduating. Three months later I was a Junior DevOps Engineer; today I'm a DevOps Engineer working across two enterprise clients.

For **Suzuki Digital** I own security, compliance and cost across a multi-account AWS organisation: consolidating 70+ accounts with Terraform, running cloud security posture management with Security Hub and GuardDuty, building a SIEM on Wazuh, and supporting CIS, ISO 27001 and SOC 2 controls. For **Flipspace** I run the full DevOps lifecycle of a multi-environment Amazon EKS platform: clusters, CI/CD on Azure Pipelines, monthly production releases, observability with Prometheus, Grafana and Loki, and on-call.

Outside work I build things I want to use myself, and I run them the way I'd run production. A [password manager](/projects/vault/), a [CVE intelligence platform](/projects/pahredar/), a [class recorder](/projects/dohra/) and this site all run on free tiers, managed with [Terraform from one repository](/projects/multi-cloud-iac/). Zero cost is a constraint, not an excuse: everything is infrastructure as code, version-controlled, tested in CI and documented well enough that a stranger could rebuild it.

Right now I'm preparing for the **CKA**, then the **CKS**.

items.title: Pahredar v1
items.body: Every published CVE, enriched and synced hourly, with security news and an endpoint scanner.

items.title: DevOps Engineer at VA2PT
items.body: Security, compliance and cost for Suzuki Digital; end-to-end DevOps for Flipspace.

items.title: Infrastructure as code, always
items.body: If it isn't in Terraform and Git, it doesn't exist. Every provider and setting is reviewable and reproducible.

items.title: Assume the server is hostile
items.body: Security is designed in, not bolted on: Vault encrypts in the browser; the assessment platform never runs candidate code on its API server.

items.title: Boring beats clever
items.body: Something that fails loudly and restarts is better than something elegant that needs nursing at 2am.

items.title: Document for a stranger
items.body: READMEs, architecture docs and decision records good enough that someone with no context can change things safely.

items.title: Tests before trust
items.body: CI runs unit and browser tests on every change; releases verify their hashes and roll back on failure.

items.title: Free tiers, real quality
items.body: Verify free-tier limits in the provider's own docs before placing a workload — then build it properly anyway.

items.title: CKA, then CKS
items.body: Kubernetes certification, with a hands-on lab kept in its own repository.

items.title: Pahredar: attack-surface monitoring
items.body: Growing from CVE tracking into watching your own internet-facing estate: passive signals first, then recon-driven scanning.

items.title: Vault editions
items.body: Personal and Business editions from one codebase, with a one-command install for your own server.

items.title: Teaching on the learn site
items.body: A free Docker course, lesson by lesson, with quizzes at the end of each.
